HSTU uses pointwise SiLU attention, A = SiLU(QKᵀ + relative position/time bias), followed by normalized value aggregation and multiplicative gating: W[LayerNorm(AV) ⊙ U]. Attention coefficients are not softmax probabilities; output effects depend jointly on content projections, aggregation, normalization, gating and residual paths. [Original HSTU paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=xye7iNsgXn).

Architectural inference: replacing a nonpadding item at the same sequence position preserves sequence length, padding layout, causal visibility and relative positional offsets. Temporal biases remain unchanged only if timestamps and their indexing also remain fixed. Replacement changes the item embedding and downstream content-dependent computations; it does not hold attention or gates constant. Resulting score/rank changes measure computational sensitivity to that particular substitution, conditional on its context and replacement choice. They do not isolate positional bias, attention, gating, or an unobserved user trait.

Stronger mechanism-level claims need targeted internal interventions: cache original/replacement activations, patch selected Q/K/V/U streams, aggregation outputs or residual states, and measure restoration or disruption of a defined candidate-score margin. Complement restoration with ablation, multiple replacement controls and replication across users/positions. Patching provides evidence about specific internal causal contributions, but conclusions depend on corruption choices, intervention sites and metrics; localization alone does not establish a complete mechanism. [Activation-patching best practices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042), [interpretation guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255).
